jobs.description: For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:Postdoctoral researcher for X-ray microscopy at atomic resolutionRemuneration Group 13 | Limited: 2 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FSPO009/2026 | Deadline: 09.12.2026 | Full-time/Part-timeDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.The Advanced Multilayer X-ray Optics group at CFEL is one of the leading research groups developing novel X-ray lenses, also known as multilayer Laue Lenses (MLLs). We plan to further improve and extend MLLs as part of a large project to image, understand and ultimately control electron dynamics in molecular systems. At the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, we bridge the gap between basic research and translational, preclinical approaches. Here, researchers from the fields of biology, chemistry, physics, and medicine collaborate across disciplines, supported by high-performance service facilities and a modern research infrastructure. As the largest institute of the Max Planck Society, with around 1,000 employees from more than 66 nations, we offer an inspiring, international working environment with exceptional scientific breadth.The research group Ubiquitin Signaling Specificity (Dr. Sonja Lorenz) invites applications for the position asPostdoc (f/m/d)- Cryo-EM Analyses of Ubiquitin Ligase Complexes - Our laboratory aims to understand how the posttranslational modifier ubiquitin coordinates eukaryotic physiology. A major key lies in the action of ubiquitin ligases that recruit specific substrates for ubiquitination and determine which ubiquitin signals they are decorated with. The immense potential of ubiquitin ligases for therapeutic applications has been illustrated by the clinical efficacy of immunomodulatory drugs in the treatment of hematological malignancies and recent advances with PROTACs and molecular glues. However, efficient targeting of ubiquitin ligases in the clinic is still limited by our insufficient understanding of their structural mechanisms, regulation, and integration into cellular pathways.We offer a Postdoc position focusing on revealing structural mechanisms of specificity, regulation, and substrate recognition by ubiquitin ligases. Available projects center on cryo-EM as a principle structural tool, but may also integrate other structural techniques, including X-ray crystallography, as well as biophysical and biochemical analyses of enzymatic activities and protein interactions. For a representative example of our integrated research approach, please seeNat Struct Mol Biol. 2024 Feb;31(2):364-377. doi: 10.1038/s41594-023-01203-4Candidates should hold/soon expect a PhD or equivalent degree in a relevant area of the life sciences. A strong published track record in single-particle cryo-EM (or cryo-ET) and in protein biochemistry is essential. The successful candidate should be curiosity-driven, creative, and passionate about science. A high degree of self-motivation and independence is important, as well as the ability to communicate well within an international, multidisciplinary team. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of extension. Remuneration is based on the TVöD Bund (German federal civil service pay scale), depending on qualifications and professional experience. In addition, public sector social benefits apply.We are committed to being a cosmopolitan institute that offers a diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities. We also aim to increase the number of employees with disabilities. We welcome applications from all backgrounds.A stimulating and collaborative international research environmentProfessional development opportunities, skills training, and the Max Planck Society’s online training academySupport for balancing work and family life, including on-campus childcare placesCorporate health management, fitness and sports programsspacious on-site cafeteria offering warm meals and a salad barSustainability initiatives and a nature-oriented campus environment, including the BioDiversum biotope projectAbout usBased at one of Germany’s premier research campuses, our research group has access to leading-edge infrastructure in all areas of cell and structural biology, including cryo-EM and superresolution imaging. We are an ambitious international team, supported by the Max Planck Society, the German Research Foundation, among other sources. Our working language is English; knowledge of German is not required. jobs.description: Key Responsibilities Briese Chartering is an established Shipowner/Carrier based in Leer/Germany managing a modern and versatile fleet of short-sea and multipurpose (MPP) vessels ranging from 3,000 to 10,000 DWT with a strong focus on carriage of project cargo. For further information see: www.briese-chartering.com (http://www.briese-chartering.com/)   We are seeking an experienced Chartering Broker to join our Intra-Europe Regional Trade desk. In this role you will hold commercial responsibility for maximizing the utilization and profitability of our owned and controlled tonnage. You will optimize vessel loops across Europe, securing high-yielding regional breakbulk and specialized project cargo stems by maintaining direct relationships with industrial charterers, shippers and project forwarders.Negotiate charter parties directly with cargo owners and competitive brokers, protecting the company's commercial interests. Fleet Optimization & Chartering Fix our 3,000–10,000 DWT fleet on Voyage Charters and Contracts of Affreightment (COAs) across European trade routes (Baltic, North Sea, Continent, Mediterranean/Black Sea and North/West Africa). Optimize vessel routing and scheduling to minimize ballast days and maximize daily time charter equivalent returns.Project Cargo & Voyage Estimation Evaluate and price specialized project cargo inquiries tailored to our vessels' capabilities. Perform precise voyage calculations including bunker tracking, port/terminal expenses, and laytime analysis to ensure optimal margins. Market Integration & Collaboration Leverage the north/central European shipping community while managing an active network of international chartering contacts. Work closely with our in-house operations and technical management teams in Leer to guarantee smooth post-fixture execution. Qualifications & Experience  Essential Criteria - Minimum 3 years of commercial experience on the owner’s side or with an exclusive broker specifically within the European short-sea or small-MPP sectors. - Solid understanding of 3k–10k DWT vessel capabilities including stowage configurations, deck strength and regional port/canal restrictions. - Deep knowledge of European trades including seasonal weather factors, ice clauses and short-sea port operations. - Fluency in English is required; proficiency in German is highly preferred given our regional hub and team integration. Core Skills - Commercial drive with a clear focus on asset P&L and strategic fleet positioning. - Proficiency in voyage estimation and other standard software tools (MS Office, Sedna, Netpas, etc.). - Existing network of direct project cargo clients, industrial shippers and European forwarders.Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Verhandlungsführung, Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnung, SchifffahrtsrechtExpertenkenntnisse: Befrachtung
